defects.repro: upload_path('/', 'a/b.txt') raises ValueError('name escapes the base directory') instead of returning '/a/b.txt'. The check uses root + os.sep, which is '//' when base is '/'. Test: qa/test_qa.py::StorageQA::test_d1_root_base_nested_name.
defects.fix: Compare with os.path.commonpath([root, path]) == root, or strip the trailing separator before building the prefix.
defects.if_skipped: Any nested upload under a root base ('/') is wrongly rejected.

defects.repro: find('ann', 'z'*50000) raises sqlite3.OperationalError: LIKE or GLOB pattern too complex. The pattern is user-controlled and long; the contract allows only ValueError for invalid input. Test: qa/test_qa.py::CatalogueQA::test_d2_large_search_text.
defects.fix: Use instr(lower(name), lower(?)) > 0 instead of LIKE, or reject over-long text with ValueError.
defects.if_skipped: A user can trigger an unhandled sqlite3.OperationalError with a very long search text, which can surface as a 500 to callers.

gaps: Symlink-based escape from the base cannot be tested: upload_path does not touch the disk (the architecture excludes writing files).

items: I did not run the unit or acceptance suites, because other stages cover them.
I did not review tests/test_*.py or acceptance/ in detail.
upload_path does not resolve symlinks. Writing files is out of scope, so a symlink inside base could still point outside it once a caller writes there.
upload_path with base '/' would wrongly reject nested names, because the root + os.sep prefix becomes '//'. I judged this unrealistic and did not report it.
Tracked __pycache__ .pyc files show as modified in git. This predates the change and I did not report it.
